title: Prove Hadamard column completion for two-prime odd alphabets
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof. Let `A` be an `n`-by-`(n-1)` partial Butson matrix over the `m`th roots, with `m = p^a q^b` for distinct odd primes. If `3 <= n < pq` and `n` is divisible by either prime, the normalized missing column uses only `m`th roots and preserves every supplied column. At any `n >= 3`, the same conclusion holds if projection to either prime-power factor preserves column orthogonality.

Below `pq`, divisibility forces every vanishing column inner product to split into cycles of the dividing prime. Projecting to that prime-power component preserves these cancellations. Reduction modulo the discarded prime then separates positive and negative roots in the recovered column. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas and answers a subcase of the odd-composite question. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718465)

Credit PR #5865 for the normalized column and prime-power sign results, David Ganz for atlas B097 and the pilot application, and Lam and Leung for the two-prime cycle decomposition. [PR #5865](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5865) · [Atlas B097](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2849) · [Lam and Leung](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9511209#page=7)

## Evidence

Both registered modes passed locally on CPython 3.12.15 using the standard library. Each checked six mixed-phase fixtures, 86 erasures, 1,574 recovered entries and their opposite signs. The controls show that mixed cycles can fail to project and that neither projection is guaranteed at `n = pq`. Each direct run took 0.03 seconds locally. Committed bytes and source history passed for all five package files.

Run from the repository root.

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/two-prime-column-completion/verify.py
python3.12 -I -W error -B -O research/two-prime-column-completion/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-prime-column-completion
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-prime-column-completion --check-source-history
```

The direct checks print `PASS_TWO_PRIME_COLUMN_COMPLETION`. The package and committed-byte checks print `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

The theorem concerns exact recovery of one column. Mixed-cycle row counts may require a different argument. Noisy recovery, physical execution, supplier pricing and independent human or formal proof-kernel review remain open. The selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were unrun. The proof establishes no new κ.

## Open next questions

- Resolve the eight-row case over the fifteenth roots. Start by dephasing the first column and using the one-three-cycle and one-five-cycle condition on every pair of column differences. A mixed vanishing sum by itself supplies no valid partial matrix.

## Related open work

The live PR and Discussion searches found no open PR on the same missing-column alphabet question. The merged proof in #5865 leaves the odd-composite case open. [PR #5865](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5865)

Two-way. The diff adds one isolated research package with no shared executable changes.
